title: How to Make a Meme and Download It as a PNG
description: Add top and bottom captions to a local image, adjust font size and color, preview and download a PNG, and fix image loading errors or clipped captions.
content:
Open the Meme Generator, select a local image, and enter a caption in Top Text or Bottom Text. Adjust Font Scale and Color, then select Generate Meme. Verify the caption placement in Preview and select Download PNG. Generate the meme again after changing the text, font scale, or color.

Create a meme from a single image

Use the sample cat image in the screenshots and look for space at the top and bottom. Enter “Ready to get to work” at the top and “Time for a break” at the bottom. After selecting the image, try the default font scale and color to see how the captions look against the original background.

Follow the steps below. Verify both the status message and the image beneath it. Make sure the image shows the captions you just entered. You can also fill in just the top or bottom field.

  1. Select a local image in the Image & Text panel.
  2. Enter a top or bottom caption and adjust Font Scale and Color as needed.
  3. Select Generate Meme. When “Meme generated” appears, verify the preview and select Download PNG.

Choose an image with room for captions

Scale the source image down to the size you typically see in chat. Look at where the eyes, gestures, or action appear. If the cat's ears are close to the upper edge, leave the top field blank and place the caption over the table at the bottom. Extra space at the sides is of little use because the tool centers each caption horizontally.

If the image already contains text, find a clear area before choosing a caption field. Leave enough space around objects you want readers to see. The tool draws the image on a canvas with the same width and height as the decoded image. It overlays captions directly on the image without adding caption bars at either edge.

Choose between a top and bottom caption

If the joke needs a setup, put it at the top and the reply at the bottom. Read each line to see whether it makes sense outside the chat. If the action already provides the setup, add a single line for the outcome and leave the other field blank. The tool trims leading and trailing whitespace and treats a field that contains only spaces as empty. If you select an image and leave both fields blank, the tool generates an image without captions and displays “Meme generated”.

Change one caption position at a time for an easier comparison. To move “Time for a break” to the top, clear the original bottom caption before generating again. See whether the caption covers empty space or the cat's expression, and verify that it appears where you want readers to see it.

Fix clipped captions

The tool wraps text based on its rendered width. The maximum line width is the source image width minus 24 pixels. Wrapped lines in the top caption extend down into the image and can cover the subject. Lines in the bottom caption also extend downward. If they run out of space, the last line can touch the edge or get clipped. Captions with the same character count can wrap at different points because character widths vary.

Start with a short phrase that conveys the same idea. For example, shorten “I just said I'd get to work, but now I want to lie down a little longer” to “A quick lie-down before work”. Generate the meme again and look for the last character along the bottom edge of the preview. If you need to keep the wording, try moving part of the caption to the top. Verify that the top caption leaves the important parts of the image visible.

How image width affects font size

The slider sets font size as a proportion of the source image width. Its range is 0.05 to 0.2, with a default of 0.1. The tool multiplies the image width by this value and rounds the result, with a minimum of 16 pixels. For example, an image 640 pixels wide has a default font size of 64 pixels. The same slider position can produce a different font size when you select an image of a different width.

If the text looks crowded, move the slider a little to the left and generate again. See whether the caption now fits on one line and remains readable at a smaller preview size. With a narrow image, moving the slider left may have no visible effect. If the font size reaches the minimum, shorten the caption or use a wider source image.

Choose a color based on the background

The Color control sets the fill for both captions and keeps the black outline. The default fill is white. On a background with light and dark areas, read across the full line and see whether strokes stay legible as they cross from dark to light. W3C's contrast guidance identifies the difference in brightness between text and its background as a factor in readability. [S4]

If the top and bottom backgrounds differ substantially, generate a few versions with a shared fill color for both captions and compare the harder-to-read line. If changing the color still leaves it hard to read, move that caption to the side with a clearer background. Move the text between the fields and generate again to see the effect. If a caption overlaps a window frame or the edge of a table, read along that edge before deciding whether to change the image. Reduce the image to chat size to spot strokes that appear to merge.

Which version the tool downloads

Download PNG saves the last image generated successfully. If you download immediately after editing a caption, the file may still show the old text. The same applies when you select a different image. Verify that the preview shows the right image and captions before saving. The preview has a maximum width of 480 pixels and scales wider images down. Open the downloaded PNG at its original size to verify the font size. The suggested filename is clover-meme.png. You can find the saved file in your browser's download history. [S5]

Open the saved image and verify the beginning and end of the text. Look for clipping at the top and bottom. If you need another file format, use the Image Converter and inspect the edges of the text in the converted file. For a smaller attachment, use Image Compression to save a separate copy so you can compare it with the original export.

What to do when an error appears

Read the message below the Image & Text panel. Selecting a file, generating a preview, and saving the file in the browser are separate steps. Follow the message and verify the preview so you can identify the current result.

MessageWhen it appearsWhat to do
Please select an image firstYou select Generate Meme without selecting an image.Select an image and generate again.
Failed to load imageThe browser could not load the selected file.Try opening the source image in a local image viewer, or select an image you know opens.
Please generate a meme firstYou select Download PNG before generating an image.Select Generate Meme, verify the preview, and then save.

If you still see the old image after selecting a new one, look for a fresh “Meme generated” message. If the image fails to load, the tool displays an error and the last successful preview may remain visible. Verify details from the new image in the preview before saving.

Scope and limitations

Before using someone else's image or meme, verify that the copyright permission covers editing and sharing. If the image shows people, also consider portrait rights and confirm that they consent to this use and sharing.

The tool loads the source image from a local file object in the browser and draws the image and captions together. A W3C example also shows how to display a local image in the browser using an object URL. [S3] The captions become part of the PNG's pixels. To edit them, return to the generator and use the original image. If you select the exported image as the source, it will still contain the old captions.

The tool downloads a static PNG. The PNG specification covers both static and animated images. The tool serializes the canvas bitmap to produce a still image for chat. [S1][S2] If you need to keep the animation in the source, save the original separately and verify which file is the static export before sharing.

Make room for both captions on a wide image

A wide image can be short, but the font size still depends on its width. When you put both captions on a wide screenshot, look for enough space between them to see the image itself. If the top caption wraps and crowds the bottom caption, remove one and reduce the font size of the remaining caption.

You can also reuse the captions on an image with more space above and below the subject. If the old and new previews look about the same width, look at how much vertical space the subject takes and whether the action is still visible between the captions. This helps you tell whether the image proportions or caption length are causing the crowding.

Make multiple versions from the same image

To try two replies with different tones, generate and save the first version, then replace only the bottom caption. For example, use “Ready to get to work” at the top of both versions and “Time for a break” and “Coming right up” at the bottom, respectively. Open each export and save it with a recognizable name so you can find the right version later.

If the second version needs slightly smaller text, verify the top caption too because both captions use the same font size. You can also keep just the bottom reply and let the photo set the scene. To compare the versions, view them at similar sizes, read the captions, and pick the one you understand fastest.

Review the meme at chat size before sending

Look at the thumbnail in the message composer. Captions too close to the edge can be harder to read at this size even if they looked fine when enlarged. Read from top to bottom. Make sure the top caption leaves the expression visible, the bottom caption's last character is intact, and the image fits the message you plan to send.

If you need to make another change, return to the generator, edit the text or style, generate again, and download the result. If you've saved several copies, open the latest one from your download history and verify the new caption before selecting it to send. Keep the source image and captions separately if you want to make another version later. If you only have the export, retrieve the original image so you can edit the captions without having to deal with the old text.

faqs.q: Can I add just a bottom caption?
faqs.a: Yes. Leave Top Text blank, fill in Bottom Text, and select Generate Meme.

faqs.q: Why does the download still show the old captions?
faqs.a: Download PNG saves the last image generated successfully. After editing the captions, generate the meme again, verify the preview, and download it again.
